decidedBy: the project owner's decision of 2026-09-30 that every relationship is this project's own and BibleData's relationship rows leave the corpus — recorded on TSK-0893 — applied so that what a page says did not change the day they left
policy: A reading listed here is a descriptor clause that is not written as a relationship. Each was read by a model and never written, because BibleData's row for the same two records answered the question otherwise and a dataset's statement outranked a model's reading; one (Keturah) is listed because the dataset's row is what settled a tie between two readings of equal confidence. The dataset's rows are gone and nothing of ours has weighed these readings since, so they stay unwritten until somebody reads the verse: several say loosely what this corpus already says closely from the other end, several contradict what the owner decided from the other end, and three pairs (Zadok and Ahitub, Meraiah and Seraiah, Jedaiah and Jeshua) have nothing else. Taking an entry off the list lets the reading be written on the next load that reads its record; a record that already has relationships is read again only when its clauses change.
